requirements.judgement: Nuclear genetic information and expression control are distinguished from selective outer-membrane exchange.
Chromosomes are DNA/protein structures carrying genes, not the entire nucleus; unfamiliar gland/contractile comparisons checked.
Selectivity correctly permits regulated exchange rather than impermeability or a cell wall.
Aerobic respiratory energy transfer supports contraction, with breathing and energy creation misconceptions excluded.
Rough ER processing/transport distinguishes the network from attached ribosome chain synthesis.
Ribosomes join amino acids into proteins; role applied to unfamiliar exported-protein demand.
Two nucleotide chains coil as a double helix; opened model explicitly distinguished from normal coiling and microscopy.
Original model distinguishes phosphate, deoxyribose and base in a nucleotide from a full strand/gene/chromosome.
A–T/C–G pairing and equal-length aligned complementary sequences checked, with direction assumptions explicit.
Hydrogen bonds placed across complementary bases rather than along the sugar–phosphate backbone.
Original hydrogen-bonded strands separate before division; replication is distinguished from cell division and RNA production.
Each original template selects complementary free DNA nucleotides; each product retains one original/new strand if copying accurate.
DNA polymerase joins the new nucleotides into continuous strands; no claim it translates bases into amino acids.
Gene is a DNA length with a sequence specifying protein in the syllabus-limited model, not stored amino acids.
Defined coding/template/mRNA trace and supplied key show ordered amino acids; change in order can affect folding/function.
Nine-base fragment gives three amino acids and24-amino-acid segment72bases under explicit stop/noncoding exclusion; neither strand doubled.
RNA usually single-stranded is distinguished from the double-stranded DNA model, without asserting every RNA lacks folded regions.
Ribose/deoxyribose distinction explained as sugar identity, not base identity.
Uracil replaces thymine in RNA; complementary template exercise checked, not erroneous T→U substitution in a template.
mRNA carries nuclear gene information to cytoplasmic ribosomes; diagram/prompt preserve compartment and molecule roles.
Changed DNA base sequence is defined separately from altered amino-acid sequence or observed phenotype.
Supplied GCU/GCC alanine and GAU aspartate keys yield checked silent/replacement paths with explicit strand identities.
Protein folding/function/phenotype changes remain possible rather than inevitable; no disease or functional effect inferred from sequence alone.
Transcription generates complementary mRNA in nucleus, distinct from DNA polymerase-mediated replication.
Original compartment model transfers mRNA to cytoplasm while nuclear DNA stays; model is not a whole-cell micrograph.
Aligned tRNA anticodons3′UAC/CGA/CUA5′ complement5′AUG/GCU/GAU3′; separate tRNAs not one nine-base carrier.
Ribosome links delivered amino acids in order into a polypeptide; shortfragment key matches and does not claim a complete functional protein.
Expressible DNA, restriction-enzyme cutting, ligase joining, plasmid uptake/selection and expression are distinct; unfamiliar plasmid-present/protein-absent evidence rejects automatic production.
Insulin is the bacterial protein product recovered and purified, not the plasmid/gene itself; expression/output check addresses the given failure.
Hepatitis B antigen protein and intended immune response are distinguished; insertion alone establishes neither antigen output nor effective vaccination.
Beta-carotene in edible endosperm is a vitamin A precursor; measured crop product does not by itself prove adequate intake or a nutritional health improvement.
Growth increases cell number by mitosis while preserving the chromosome set; original multi-use prompt requires the specific role.
Repair replaces lost/damaged cells with normally matching genetic information rather than halving chromosomes.
Cloning expands genetically matching cells from a starting source, with mutation qualification and no meiosis claim.
Mitotic asexual reproduction retains parental information without gamete fusion; lesson excludes bacterial division from mitosis.
Condensed duplicated chromosomes and forming spindle identify prophase in an unfamiliar verbal image; nuclear-envelope breakdown is separately explained.
Four duplicated X-shaped chromosomes aligned at the equator identify metaphase; X/centromere counting separates chromosomes from chromatids.
Separated sisters moving to opposite poles identify anaphase, distinct from an aligned metaphase or mere spindle visibility.
Re-forming nuclear envelopes identify telophase; nuclear re-formation remains distinct from cytoplasmic separation.
Original four/eight-chromosome examples preserve the diploid set in each daughter, not total across daughters; normal-copy/no-mutation assumptions explicit.
Embryonic cells have broad body-cell differentiation potential; scenario uses multiple cultured types without treating that observation as therapeutic success.
Adult tissue stem cells have a more restricted tissue-related potential; table comparison does not misclassify reprogrammed iPSC as ordinary adult stem cells.
Broad differentiation supports developmental and cell-based research; unfamiliar proposal benefit is balanced against missing recipient evidence.
Control of growth, integration and sustained function remain unproved in the scenario, with immune matching identified as a possible difficulty.
Embryo destruction and moral status remain ethically disputed even with voluntary consent; neither view is stated as a proven biological fact.
Adult tissue-related potential, avoidance of embryo destruction and possible autologous matching benefit are qualified rather than guaranteed.
Restricted range and small starting supply can constrain adult-cell use; differentiation does not establish effective long-term function.
Adult donor consent, collection welfare and fair access are assessed separately from the embryo issue; consent does not erase every harm.
Cell groups with related functions form tissues; unfamiliar gland prompt correctly orders cell, tissue and organ without relying on size.
Stomach/gland examples connect distinct secretory, muscle/supply and coordinating/supporting tissues to cooperation; no assertion of a single-tissue organ.
Labelled flagellum provides propulsion; original immobile-tail comparison separates reaching the egg from penetration.
Midpiece mitochondria transfer energy for tail movement; unfamiliar reduced-mitochondria case avoids energy creation or an inevitable diagnosis.
Acrosome enzymes contribute to surrounding-layer penetration, distinct from the nucleus; normally moving/acrosome-impaired contrast assessed.
Egg cytoplasm contains organelles/resources for earliest development; model and text explicitly exclude food supply for the whole human pregnancy.
Post-fertilisation changes help prevent further sperm entry and extra chromosome sets; surrounding layers are labelled without a false physical scale.
Haploid nuclei each contribute one set; independent six-plus-six example gives diploid twelve, with egg size not determining ploidy.
